subject: Post-demo: transactional truncate policy & residency follow-ups
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Aliya Khan <aliya.khan@clearline.io>
Cc: Daniel Morris <dan.morris@clearline.io>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: transactional truncate policy & residency follow-ups

Hi Aliya / Daniel —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from my side and next steps we discussed on the call: 

- Goal: allow Clearline to run clinical text enrichment with Redwood while meeting your PII minimization and residency constraints.
- Key asks you raised: 1) ability to truncate/strip sensitive fields at ingestion for certain transaction types, 2) EU residency for patient identifiable flows, 3) documented proof points (SOC2, audit logs), and 4) an API to trigger on-demand purge for flagged sessions.

What we can offer as a starting point (we covered these on the demo):
- Transactional truncate policy: per-route config that drops or tokenizes specified JSON fields at the edge (zero bytes written to KV) OR keeps a reduced KV footprint for up to N days.
- Residency: run the pipeline in eu-central-1 for EU traffic; cross-region fallback only with explicit allowlist.
- Evidence: SOC2 report + sample audit log snippet for model inference events (redacted).
- On-demand purge: REST endpoint to trigger synchronous purge of KV and cached prefixes for a session id (we need to agree SLA for purge propagation).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I’ll loop in our privacy lead (Aditya Rao) and solutions engineer (Ben Carter) to draft a short appendix that sketches the transactional truncate policy and the purge API contract.
2) Clearline to share a short example payload for a patient-facing endpoint so we can validate tokenization rules.
3) We’ll follow up with draft clause language for the CLA that captures a 0-retention option for DSPEC-marked fields.

I attached the demo recording and the quick diagram we walked through.

Attachments: demo-recording-20270420.mp4 (recording link), demo-truncate-diagram.png (diagram)

Thanks — talk soon.

Kimberly Park

Also, we’ll need a short list of the evidence items your security team can share publicly (SOC2 date/version, penetration test timeframe) — legal asked for those up front.

Finally, we can share a sample JSON representing our patient intake payload (PHI redacted in this email). Expect that by Monday.

Hi Aliya / Daniel —

Appreciate the sample payload — that was super helpful. Attached is a concise appendix describing two options we propose for your transactional flows, plus an operational spec for the on-demand purge API. Summary below: 

Option A — Truncate-at-ingest (strict):
- Behavior: configured fields are stripped at edge; no model K/V or cached prefix is persisted.
- Audit/logging: request_id-level audit entries retained (request metadata only; payload fields redacted).
- Use case: high-risk PHI fields (SSN, patient_name, raw_notes).
- Limitations: no replay for debugging; we provide a limited debug-mode that requires a signed, scoped support request.

Option B — Reduced-horizon storage (7-day compact):
- Behavior: specified fields are tokenized and stored in compacted form for up to 7 days; metadata retained for feature reconstruction.
- Audit/logging: full inference trace available to your security team for the 7-day window; payloads redacted per DSPEC markers.
- Use case: ephemeral features where short replay is needed for model tuning.

Purge API (operational spec):
- Endpoint: POST /v1/admin/purge-session
- Inputs: session_id, route_id, scope (kv|cache|all)
- Ack: 60s
- Target propagation: 99th percentile within 10 minutes for single-region workloads; up to 60 minutes in cross-region failover scenarios.
- Audit: purge_event logged with actor, timestamp, and verification token.

Residency / SLA:
- Routes can be pinned to a region (eu-central-1) with a regional isolation SLA: cross-region fallback allowed only for explicit failover triggered by health check failures; fallback rate will be measurable and included in the CLA appendix.

Evidence bundle we can share: current SOC2 report (v2026.3), pentest summary (Q1 2027), and a redacted audit log sample. We’ll provide links in the DocuSign appendix.

Attachments to this email: proposed_truncate_appendix.pdf (2 pages), on_demand_purge_api_spec.md (API details), redlines_Clearline_CLA.docx (initial clause language).

Next steps we propose:
1) Clearline to confirm whether you want Option A (strict) for all patient-facing routes or a hybrid (A for PHI, B for behavioral telemetry).
2) Legal to review redlined CLA and confirm the regional isolation metric you need (we proposed <=0.1% cross-region fallback monthly).
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Ben to validate the payload sample and test the tokenization rules (propose Thu 29 Apr 10:00 AM BST).

If that plan looks good I’ll push the DocuSign bundle and send calendar invites.

Best —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
